correctness.rationale: Finite-edge projection exactly reduces squared clearance to the sum of the d-1 smallest squared i.i.d. uniform face gaps. An ordered-ball integral proves the two-term law, its sole first-clipping excess and positive beta-integral singular coefficient. The d=3 explicit CDF follows by splitting the elementary ordered-pair integral. A shrinking simplex at the cube center proves the upper tail; a squared-maximum identity gives the exact second moment. A standalone checker independently verified geometry and formula numerically across d=3..8 and 1.2 million simulations. These finite checks are corroborative, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The edge skeleton of a hypercube is a canonical geometric object and Euclidean clearance to it is a natural distribution with tangible relevance to grid-frame spacing. The first face-clipping threshold is geometrically mandated, and its sharp singularity differentiability exponent in every dimension is a structural boundary phenomenon rather than a small numerical gain. The complete elementary cube CDF and opposite sharp center-tail constant give a self-contained global picture beyond the known short-cylinder polynomial.
